references.text: Balak, king of Moab, sent a message to Balaam in Aram to curse Israel, which forms the background for Balaam's statement here.
Balaam lifts his voice again with a similar utterance (mashal), showing a recurring pattern in his prophecies.
Refers to how Balak brought Balaam from Aram to curse Israel, but God turned the curse into a blessing.
Paddan-Aram is mentioned as an area in the east (Mesopotamia), confirming the geographical location of Balaam's homeland.
The lands of the east and the mountains in the east refer to the same region from which Balaam came.
Micah reminds Israel of Balak's plans and Balaam's response, showing God's faithfulness to His people.
Balak rebuked Balaam because he blessed instead of cursing, showing that the mission was to curse Jacob/Israel.
